evals.prompt: Write a short message to a teammate. You tested a PDF processing feature. One heavy PDF with large images caused the image model to fail and stopped the pipeline; several other PDFs worked. You have a telemetry trace but no URL to share in this exercise. Ask whether the teammate wants to own the fix or wants you to investigate further. Do not invent other findings.
evals.expected_output: A direct teammate message that gives context, the observed failure, the limit of testing, and a useful next question without making up a trace or broader impact.
expectations: States that only one tested PDF failed while others worked
Does not invent a URL, root cause beyond the supplied evidence, or a fix
Uses a natural teammate tone rather than a formal announcement

evals.prompt: Explain to machine-learning classmates why a fictional digit classifier with 99% test accuracy should not automatically grade handwritten exam scores. Its errors include some handwritten 7s read as 1s. Low-confidence predictions could be sent for manual review. Keep it around 150 words and do not invent more measurements.
evals.expected_output: A technically careful explanation that translates the accuracy number into consequences, uses a concrete example, and explains a mitigation without claiming that confidence catches every error.
expectations: Connects 99% accuracy to roughly one error per 100 predictions under comparable test conditions
Uses the 7-versus-1 example and explains why an exam score matters
Offers manual review for low-confidence predictions without claiming all mistakes are caught

evals.prompt: Draft a social post for a fictional research project that reads handwritten exam scores. Supplied facts: it scored 92 correct out of 100 on a controlled set and 83 out of 100 on a small batch of real teacher sheets. Handwritten 7s were sometimes read as 1s. The team is testing a manual-review step for uncertain predictions. No code or dataset has been released. Make the post useful on its own and do not invent details.
evals.expected_output: An honest, self-contained research post with the two scores shown together, a concrete error example, a limitation, and a next step; no invented release, hype, or emojis.
expectations: Presents both controlled and real-sheet results together with their scope
Names the 7-versus-1 failure and the proposed manual-review step
Does not claim the project is solved, released, or ready for deployment
